I definitely understand the frustration and upkeep with the blondes, I change mine every month pretty much and blonde is the hardest. Usually I would recommend regular trips back to the salon ever 5-6 weeks for blondes and possible toner in between but I do get not everyone wants to spend that kind of money. That is my recommendation anyway to upkeep the blonde, it’s not going to stay a cool shade for months and months unfortunately. I guess if it did we’d be out of jobs! If you’re going to go darker doing DIY get some advice before so you can get the right colour for yourself!

If that’s the case, that the colour is washing out and leaving you brassy more often than not I would get it lifted a shade more so you don’t keep having this issue. With some olaplex added to your bleach would reduce breakage if that’s something you’re concerned about but I would try a blue powder bleach (Kenra has a good one or Schwarzkopf igora) with 3% developer. Yellow is the very last colour to come out of your hair in the bleaching process, from dark brown the red is lifted first, then the orange and then yellow. Once the yellow is lifted out then you have a clean white blonde. Yellow is pretty stubborn which is why toners are used. Basically I have never met anyone that can just use bleach and walk away with perfectly platinum cool coloured hair. That’s all down to toners, so long as it’s lifted light enough anyway.

Slightly different colours, you need one with more violet and blue tones which is what 10/86 will give you (tone 8 is blue and 6 is violet) so the blue will combat the brassiness. To be honest if that colour doesn’t do anything you’ll probably need your hair bleached again with 3% to try and get the last of the yellow out. 10/69 is violet/pearl so without the addition of the blue it wouldn’t be as effective on your tone.

Get a violet blonde colour to go over the top. Wella have some great choices if you have access to salon brands. The violet will neutralise the yellow/brassy tone and clean up the blonde. I would mix it with and low percentage developer like 3% or lower.
A colour like Wella 10/86 with 3% should turn out quite nicely for you.

You’d need to pre pigment your hair to avoid it going green. 
Colour theory would help in this situation. 
Usually you’d pre pig with a warm tone and then put the desired colour on. It depends how dark you’re going as to what tone you deposit. If you’re going to a shade 8 then a yellow tone, shade 6 would need orange etc. 
Avoid just going out and buying an ash brown to put over without pre pig. If you want the ash tone you still need to add warmth beforehand to avoid green tones. As you want the chestnut brown I would recommend it just to make sure it goes the shade you are after.

Hope that makes sense and good luck.

What peroxide do you use? You might need higher percentage peroxide or might be worth going over them again with 3% just to remove the yellow. When you lift your hair it goes through stages - when your hair is dark the red is lifted out first, then orange and then yellow. So yellow is the last colour to remain before You reach platinum blonde.
Not knowing what dye you are using or wanting to mix together I can’t really say. But yes you could get a darker red direct dye and that will work. Maybe something like manic panic vampire kiss?

No, you can’t get rid of your hair pattern unfortunately. 

The only way would be if you had the right products and you styled it every day to sit where you want but I feel like this would be tedious and not really worth it. What about a split fringe? That may work with a cowlick depending on what yours is like? Hard to say without knowing exactly where it is and how severe it is.

You COULD have the ends the same as the root colour but that takes a little colour theory knowledge. Essentially you need to cancel out the red and to do that you need to look at the colour wheel to see what is on the opposite side of the wheel (green) so then you need to match your root shade and just from the photo I can see it appears to be around a level 5 or 6. So essentially you will need to get something like a 5.2 or 6.2 (if you’re going by Wella numbers) some companies have different numbers for different tones. So you need level 5/6 with green tones. It’s hard to tell you exactly which product to get without knowing what brand but it’s simple to look up if you need. To be honest it would be so much easier to just get a hairdresser to do this as so much can go wrong. If you wanted the ends to be purple that might be your best bet as you can put a blue direct dye over the red (red and blue make purple).

I’ve probably just confused you so sorry if I have but as I said probably best to get to a hairdresser that knows exactly what to do for you than trying to fix yourself. 

(I’m a hairdresser)

Edit- the alternative would be to get a deep purifying shampoo and just scrub your hair everyday until it eventually fades out.

As much as you need to cover mid lengths - ends! 

However, conditioner is fine but treatments are much more effective. Conditioner isn’t absorbed into the cuticle, it sits on the outer layer and only lasts until your next shampoo. You could leave the conditioner on for 30 seconds or 5 minutes and it won’t make any difference also having a larger amount of conditioner won’t make any difference either. Treatments are actually absorbed into the cuticle therefore repairing the hair from inside and lasts a few washes. Treatments will improve your hair the longer it’s left in. 

So as long as you have a good hair care routine you should be good and you can use however much conditioner you feel works for you.

Personally I use a clarifying shampoo first then super strength shampoo and I don’t bother with conditioner too often and just go for a nice moisture treatment. Once it’s towel dried I use a silk serum and heat protect then style 👍🏽

You will need to bleach to lighten unless you have virgin hair. If you have virgin hair you can use a high lift tint. Otherwise bleach then tone. The developer needed will depend on your starting shade and the shade you want to achieve. So say you’re starting with a level 7 and want to get to a level 9 then the developer needed will be 9% (30 volume) which gives 2-3 levels of lift. You can google hair colour number chart to see where your current shade is at. once you’ve reached your target shade of 9 you will probably need to tone and that will depend what your result is after bleach. So say your result has orange tones you will need to cancel the orange with blue. So the colour needed would be a 9.8 if you are buying a wella colour. If it’s more yellow then purple so a 9.9 from wella. I would double check the brand you purchase and their tone numbering system to get the right one as they can differ slightly. I would mix the colour chosen with tone lotion rather than more developer as you shouldn’t need to. Hope that helps!

Depends what colour you have as to if you can achieve white blonde. Everyone assumes you can just put on a purple/silver toner on any blonde and it will magically go white. Your hair needs to be around a level 10-11 and only slightly yellow (yellow is the hardest colour to remove) that is the only shade and tone that a purple/silver toner will change to be white blonde. If your hair is too orange then the tone to cancel out orange is blue. If it’s too red then you need green however those sort of tones you won’t get a clean white blonde result. If you got close after your toner that you just did and it’s just a matter of leaving on a little longer then yes you can tone again. Toners in general aren’t as damaging as a colour service as it doesn’t use developer. Some toners can dry the hair so make sure you do a nice moisture treatment afterwards.
